Camila — thanks for the summary. A few specific clarifications Legal has asked for: 

1) Backups: If a user is deleted, are they removed from backups automatically or is there a window where the data could be restored from a backup image? We need language we can put in our DPA.
2) Metadata/logs: What logging do you retain (request metadata, IPs, timestamps) and for how long? Is there an option to disable request-level logging for regulated customers?

Also, Legal asked whether Redwood offers an expedited purge (we’re likely to request for some sensitive accounts) and what the SLA and cost would be for that.

Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF & deletion workflow - FintechCo

Hi Sanjay / Legal team —

Thanks — below are concrete details you can use for the DPA + CISO review. I’ve attached our RTBF playbook (RTBF-workflow.pdf) and a short one-pager for Legal.

1) Active data deletion (what happens immediately):
- Deletion request triggers removal from the active customer namespace. For typical object & vector stores we remove pointers/objects within 24 hours.
- Inference logs and request traces associated with the customer are marked for deletion and are removed from active retention stores within 24 hours, unless otherwise configured by contract.
- KV caches and live inference caches are invalidated immediately.

2) Indexes & embeddings:
- Embeddings are dereferenced on delete; search indexes will be updated in the next index maintenance window. Index maintenance typically completes within 72 hours for datasets of the size you described. We do not require service downtime for this; there may be a short window where deleted vectors no longer participate in new indexing but residual references are removed during maintenance.

3) Backups & immutable snapshots:
- Standard backup retention policy: 30 days. Backups are snapshot-based. Deletion from backups occurs during the normal backup retention purge cycle and can therefore take up to 30 days for deleted items to be removed from snapshot copies.
- Expedited purge: For enterprise customers on a Private or Dedicated plan we offer an expedited purge option (subject to verification and support ticket) that initiates an accelerated cycle to redact data from backup images where feasible. Note that for offsite immutable third-party backup providers, we may be constrained by the provider's retention policies — we will surface those constraints in the SOC 2 / vendor evidence.

4) Logging & telemetry:
- By default we retain request metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts) and error traces for 90 days. IP-level logging and raw request bodies containing PII are optional and can be disabled via configuration for specific customers.
- We can provide segregated logging retention windows in the contract for regulated customers; we also support sending logs to a customer-managed SIEM via secure streaming for audit needs.

5) Evidence & docs:
- SOC 2 documentation and our deletion playbook: https://redwood.app/docs/security/soc2-report and https://drive.google.com/rtbf-playbook-id (attached).

Next steps / Options for FintechCo:
- Option A (standard): Use our standard RTBF workflow (deletes in active store in 24h; backups purged on 30d cycle).
- Option B (expedited): We open a verified expedited purge ticket (support/RTBF-4521) and coordinate with infra/legal; estimated extra cost depending on scope — typical engagements run between 8–24 engineering hours + support coordination.

If you want, I can get our Privacy lead on a short call to walk Legal through the playbook and the provider/vendor constraints for backups.

Attachments: RTBF-workflow.pdf
Links: https://redwood.app/support/tickets/RTBF-4521

Let me know if you want me to draft DPA language for the specific clauses (we can propose 30d backup retention + expedited purge addendum).

Thanks,
Camila
